title: Type confusion: a note treated as a user object
root_cause: The program is told what an object is by something the attacker controls (a message field, a JavaScript value, a cast on an untrusted pointer) instead of by the object itself. It then reads the object's bytes under a different layout, so attacker-chosen data lands where a pointer or length is expected. This is the dominant bug class in browser JavaScript engines (V8 and others) and appears in any runtime that mixes typed layouts.
defenses: Derive the type from a tag stored inside the object (or from the language's own type system) and check it before every cast.
Prefer tagged unions / sum types / sealed variants that the compiler checks (Rust enums, Java sealed classes).
Never let a message field choose which struct layout is applied to existing memory.
Use compiler type-safety flags and sanitizers (CFI, -fsanitize=undefined, ASan) in test builds.
Fuzz parsers and engine entry points; type confusion is easy to reach and hard to review by eye.
